Belt Sway Switch Working Principle: Roller Lever, Alarm and Trip Angles, PLC Wiring and Spacing

A conveyor belt that wanders off centre can tear its edge on the steelwork. A roller lever switch catches that drift in two steps, first with an alarm and then with a trip, before the damage is done.

Roller Lever Alarm & Trip NC Wiring to PLC Spacing Calculator Troubleshooting

A conveyor misalignment switch turns sideways belt drift into an alarm contact and then a trip contact. Here are its angles, PLC wiring, spacing, a drift calculator and a fault finding flowchart.

Hello everyone, today we are going to learn how a belt sway switch protects a conveyor, how its two contacts are set and wired, and how to test it in the field.
Quick Answer

What is a belt sway switch and how does it work?

Belt sway switch units are roller lever switches fitted in pairs beside a conveyor belt, with the roller just clear of the belt edge. When the belt drifts, its edge pushes the roller and the lever tilts, so a cam opens an alarm contact first (15° on the DUK unit) and a trip contact later (25°), and the PLC stops the drive.

What Is a Belt Sway Switch?

A belt sway switch is a heavy duty roller lever switch mounted beside a conveyor belt that operates when the belt edge drifts sideways and pushes the roller. It gives an early alarm at a small lever angle and stops the conveyor at a larger angle, before the belt rubs the structure and damages its edge.

Key Facts
  • Also called a belt misalignment, belt drift or run off switch, and marked BSS on plant drawings.
  • Fitted in pairs, one on each side, because the belt can drift either way.
  • Two contacts in one housing: first for alarm, second for trip.
  • Maximum lever travel is 75° in the Fine Tek SRT and DUK manuals.

You will find these switches on long belt conveyors in cement plants, steel plants, thermal power coal handling plants, ports and mines. They are one part of the protection set in our guide to conveyor safety switches and their types, alongside pull cord, zero speed and chute blockage switches.

Inside the cast housing you get a lever, a roller, a cam and two micro switches, which makes the BSS a rugged cousin of the ordinary limit switch. In the field, most problems come from how the switch is mounted, how its angles are set and how it is wired.

Do You Know?

Material spilled from a drifting belt builds up under the return idlers and around the tail pulley, and that build up can push the belt even further off centre.

Advertisement

How Does a Belt Sway Switch Work?

It turns sideways belt movement into lever rotation. The belt edge pushes a free turning roller, the lever tilts about its pivot, and a cam on the shaft operates the alarm contact first and the trip contact later.

1
Belt centred
Both rollers stand vertical with a small gap and both contacts are closed.
2
Edge touches roller
The drifting belt closes the gap and pushes the roller outward.
3
First contact
At the first cam angle the alarm micro switch changes over.
4
Second contact
If drift continues, the trip contact changes over and the conveyor stops.
5
Reset
A spring returns the lever, or the operator resets a latched model by hand.

The roller turns freely so the moving belt does not grind it, but it still wears, and Fine Tek advises replacing its touch roller after 2 mm of wear. Eaton also offers a maintained action version whose contacts stay operated until someone resets the switch, and an AFAX model for Zone 21 and 22 dust areas.

Belt Misalignment Switch Alarm and Trip Angles

Most belt misalignment switches have two actuation angles, a smaller one for alarm and a larger one for trip. The values differ between makers, so always read them from the manual of the switch you are fitting.

Switch (source)First contactSecond contactMax travel
DUK, Klinkmann manual15°25°75°
Fine Tek SRT manual20° (reset 18°)35° (reset 33°)75°
Electro Sensors BA1000 to 45° adjustable0 to 45° adjustable90° each way

The DUK manual says its leading contact acts at roughly 4 cm of belt displacement and the main contact at roughly 7 cm. You can estimate the same numbers for any switch from its lever length, where R is the pivot to roller contact distance and g is the gap left at installation.

Drift at contact = gap + lever × sin θ
d = g + R × sin θ
Example: g = 25 mm, R = 165 mm
Alarm, 15°: 25 + 165 × 0.259 = 68 mm
Trip, 25°: 25 + 165 × 0.423 = 95 mm

A 165 mm lever fits the DUK figures well, since 165 × sin 15° is about 43 mm and 165 × sin 25° is about 70 mm.

Quick Tip

Mark the alarm and trip drift on the stringer with paint during commissioning, so operators can see how close the belt runs to a trip.

Advertisement

How to Wire a Belt Sway Switch to a PLC

Wire each contact to its own PLC digital input through the NC terminals, so the input is ON when the belt is healthy. A drift, a cut cable or a loose terminal then all read as OFF and stop the conveyor.

Each micro switch has common, NO and NC terminals, the same as in pressure switch wiring with NO and NC contacts. On 24 V DC cards, check whether the input is sinking or sourcing before you decide which side of the contact gets the supply.

Fine Tek rates its standard SPDT contact at 15 A for 125 or 250 V AC but only 5 A at 30 V DC. In dusty galleries the cable gland and housing matter as much, and the Fine Tek flameproof model carries an IP67 rating.

NC contact to PLC (recommended)
  • A broken wire trips the belt
  • Loose terminal or blown fuse shows at once
  • Same fail safe logic as other conveyor trips
NO contact to PLC
  • Input turns ON only on drift
  • A cut cable stays hidden until a trip fails
  • Fit only for a non safety indication

In the PLC, give the alarm channel a message and horn, and give the trip channel an interlock that stops the drive and the feeders upstream. Add a short input filter for contact bounce, as explained in switch debouncing.

Where several switches feed one conveyor, use first out alarm logic so the HMI shows which one tripped first. This ladder logic primer covers the contacts and coils you need.

Belt edgePushes roller
Lever and camRotate
Micro switchNC opens
PLC inputGoes OFF
InterlockStops drive
Do You Know?

Many plants also take one trip contact straight into the motor starter circuit, so the belt stops even if the PLC is in program mode. Check your plant philosophy first.

Where to Install Belt Sway Switch Pairs on a Conveyor

Put a pair near the head pulley, near the tail pulley and at each loading point, then add pairs along long runs at the spacing your plant standard sets. Electro Sensors notes that its BA100 pairs usually go near the head end, with the tail and selected points as other options.

Head end
A few idlers before the head pulley, where drift is most costly.
Tail end
Just after the tail, where return side build up starts drift.
Loading point
Near each chute, since off centre loading pushes the belt over.
Long runs
Extra pairs on overland and gallery conveyors, closer on curves.

No single spacing rule fits every plant. Eaton describes its AFA switches as installed near high risk locations every 300 meters, while a Bulk Online forum user describes a 250 m conveyor with eight switches, four per side.

The DUK manual asks for the middle height of the roller to match the belt edge and for the gap to equal the drift you will accept. Electro Sensors suggests about 1 inch (25 mm) and warns that mounting too close causes false signals.

Coal dust areas need certified housings, so check the hazardous area zone of each gallery and whether the site asks for ATEX or IECEx marking.

Conveyor Switch Count and Drift Calculator

Enter the conveyor length and your pair spacing to get the switch count, and the lever data to get the drift at each contact. The defaults are the numbers from the example above.

Belt Sway Switch Count and Drift Calculator
Result
12 switches (6 pairs), alarm at 68 mm drift, trip at 95 mm drift

Pairs = length ÷ spacing, rounded up, plus one, so both ends are covered. If a pair lands in an awkward spot, shift it to the nearest loading point or curve.

Advertisement

How to Set and Test the Actuation Angle

Set the angle by adjusting the cam on the lever shaft, then tilt the roller by hand and check each contact with a meter and at the PLC. Fine Tek asks for this manual check at regular intervals, not only at commissioning.

1
Isolate
Take a permit and isolate the conveyor drive.
2
Check mounting
Roller vertical, at belt edge height and at the planned gap.
3
Set the cam
Adjust to the alarm and trip angles from the maker or design sheet.
4
Meter and PLC test
Tilt slowly, note where each NC contact opens, then confirm the alarm and trip live.
5
Record
Log angles, tag and date, then close the cover tightly.

It is the same discipline as an instrument loop check, only for a discrete device. Fine Tek warns that loose cover screws let water and dust in, and says not to lubricate the unit.

Why Does a Conveyor Keep Tripping on Belt Sway?

Repeated sway trips usually mean a real tracking problem, such as off centre loading, a misaligned idler or build up on a pulley. The rest come from the switch or its circuit, so work through the flowchart in order.

SymptomLikely causeField fix
Trips only when loadedOff centre chute loadingAlign chute and skirts
Alarm with belt centredGap too small or bent leverReset gap, straighten lever
No trip on hand testCam slipped or contact weldedReset cam or replace switch
Random trips in monsoonWater in housing or glandDry out, change gasket
Myth: The switch corrects belt tracking.
Fact: It only detects drift; tracking is fixed at idlers, pulleys and chutes.
Myth: Frequent trips mean move it further away.
Fact: That hides the fault and lets the belt reach the structure first.
Myth: NO contacts are fine for a trip.
Fact: A cut wire on an NO circuit looks healthy, so the trip never comes.
Quick Tip

After a trip, ask which side tripped and whether the belt was loaded. Those two answers usually point to the chute, the tail pulley or the switch.

For faults inside the panel, follow the PLC troubleshooting steps for the input card. Add the hand test and roller wear check to your preventive maintenance plan.

Belt Sway Switch vs Pull Cord and Zero Speed Switch

A sway switch detects sideways drift, a pull cord switch lets a person stop the belt from the walkway, and a zero speed switch detects slip or a stopped pulley. Each one watches a different fault, so a conveyor needs all three.

FeatureSway switchPull cordZero speed
DetectsBelt driftRope pulledSlow pulley
OutputAlarm and tripLatched tripRelay or pulses
MountingPairs at belt edgeAlong walkwayNon drive pulley
ResetSpring or manualManualAutomatic

Read more on the zero speed switch. Pull cord switches belong to the emergency stop function, so they follow the same latching rules as emergency stop push buttons.

  • Pairs at head, tail and loading points
  • Roller at belt edge height and planned gap
  • Angles set and recorded per tag
  • NC contacts on separate PLC inputs
  • Hand test seen on the drive

Belt Sway Switch FAQ

What is the difference between a belt sway switch and pull cord switch?

A sway switch senses belt drift on its own, while a pull cord switch is operated by a person pulling a rope along the walkway.

The sway switch usually resets with a spring, but the pull cord switch latches and needs a manual reset at the switch.

How to calculate belt drift at the alarm and trip angle step by step?

Use d = g + R × sin θ, where g is the roller gap, R the lever length and θ the contact angle.

With a 25 mm gap and 165 mm lever, the alarm at 15° acts at 68 mm drift and the trip at 25° acts at 95 mm drift.

Should sway switch contacts be wired NO or NC to a PLC input?

Wire them NC so the input is ON when the belt is healthy. A drift, a cut cable or a lost supply then all turn the input OFF and stop the conveyor.

An NO circuit hides a broken wire until a real drift fails to trip.

Why does the sway switch trip the conveyor when the belt looks fine?

Check the roller gap first, because a gap set too small lets normal belt wander reach the alarm angle. Then look for a bent lever, a slipped cam or water in the housing.

If the contact tests closed, check the cable cores and the input fuse.

Which belt sway switch type is best for a coal handling plant?

Choose a dust ignition proof model certified for the gallery zone, with IP67 sealing and at least two contacts.

A maintained version that needs a local reset helps when the plant wants a site check of the belt after every trip.

What We Learn Today

  • A belt sway switch turns sideways belt drift into lever rotation, opening an alarm contact first and a trip contact at the larger angle.
  • Belt drift at each contact follows d = g + R × sin θ, so the roller gap and lever length decide how early the switch acts.
  • Fit switches in pairs at head, tail and loading points, wire NC contacts to separate PLC inputs and test them by hand regularly.
